parts:
Hello everyone,
I am fairly new to nimble and I am trying to make my first model in order to estimate if my fish is more in a "foraging" state or in-transit. This states depends on the distance travelled every day (and associated turning angles, but I'll add complexcity when I'll figure how this works exactly) which is associated with a gamma distribution.
 My problem is that : when I try to run everything (with only one invidividual, always to keep it simple at start) I have this weird error :

"Building model Setting data and initial values Running calculate on model [Note] Any error reports that follow may simply reflect missing values in model variables. [Warning] Dynamic index out of bounds: dcat(prob = gamma[z[i, t_minus_1], 1:2]) [Warning] Dynamic index out of bounds: dcat(prob = gamma[z[i, t_minus_1], 1:2]) [Warning] Dynamic index out of bounds: 1/omega[z[i, t], 2]"

Here is my code :

'''
hmm.traj <- nimbleCode({
 
  # Prior
  ## Transition
  phi.S ~ dunif(0, 1)
  phi.NS ~ dunif(0, 1)
 
  ## Observation
  alpha.S ~ dunif(0, 1)
  beta.S ~ dunif(0, 1)
  alpha.NS ~ dunif(0, 1)
  beta.NS ~ dunif(0, 1)
 
  # Initial state probability
  delta[1] <- 0 # Pr(in-search t = 1) = 0
  delta[2] <- 1 # Pr(in-transit t = 1) = 1
 
  # Transition matrix
  gamma[1,1] <- phi.S      # Pr(in-search t -> in-search t+1)
  gamma[1,2] <- 1 - phi.S  # Pr(in-search t -> in-transit t+1)
  gamma[2,1] <- 1- phi.NS  # Pr(in-transit t -> in-search t+1)
  gamma[2,2] <- phi.NS     # Pr(in-transit t -> in-transit t+1)
   
  # Observation matrix
  omega[1,1] <- alpha.S
  omega[1,2] <- beta.S
  omega[2,1] <- alpha.NS
  omega[2,2] <- beta.NS
 
  # Likelihood
  ## Iteration over individuals
  for (i in 1:N) {
    z[i, 1] ~ dcat(delta[1:2]) # t = 1
   
    ## Iteration over time
    for (t in 2:T) {
      z[i,t] ~ dcat(gamma[z[i,t-1], 1:2])
      y[i,t] ~ dgamma(shape = omega[z[i,t], 1],
                      rate = omega[z[i,t], 2])
    } # t
  } # i
 
})

(my.constants <- list(N = 1, T = 239))
my.data <- list(y = y)

zinits <- y
initial.values <- function() list(phi.S = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  phi.NS = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  alpha.S = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  beta.S = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  alpha.NS = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  beta.NS = runif(1, 0, 1),
                                  z = zinits)

(parameters.to.save <- c("phi.S", "phi.NS",
                        "alpha.S", "beta.S",
                        "alpha.NS", "beta.NS"))

n.iter <- 5000
n.burnin <- 1000
n.chains <- 2

mcmc.output <- nimbleMCMC(code = hmm.traj,
                          constants = my.constants,
                          data = my.data,
                          inits = initial.values,
                          monitors = parameters.to.save,
                          niter = n.iter,
                          nburnin = n.burnin,
                          nchains = n.chains)
'''

Would you have some hints about how to solve this please ? (I am quite sure other problems are going to emerge, but I am stuck ith this one for quite too long..)

Have a wonderful day !
Rémy

parts:
Hi Rémy,

The message indicates that the initial values for `z` are in some way not valid indices for `gamma` and `omega`. Your initial values for `z` need to be either 1 or 2 because `gamma` and `omega` have only two rows. But you are initializing `z` (which must be 1 or 2) the same as the initial values of `y` (with y being continuous random variables), so that is presumably the cause of the problem.

-Chris

Hi Rémy,

Internally, NIMBLE reparameterizes this gamma distribution:

y[i,t] ~ dgamma(shape = omega[z[i,t], 1],
                      rate = omega[z[i,t], 2])

using the inverse of the rate parametr. That introduces a new parameter for the inverse rate (the scale parameter) named `lifted_d1_over_omega_oBz_oBi_comma_t_cB_comma_2_cB_L30`.
The message suggests that `omega` is not being correctly initialized, which causes the new parameter also not to be initialized.

From your code it looks like you are initializing things, so my suggestion is to build the model using `nimbleModel` (separately from using `nimbleMCMC`, so that you can explore what is going on), and then look at the values in the model:

model$omega
model$z

As far as your question about initializing 'z', yes, you can initialize with some random values.

-chris

If you provide some NAs for `y` via `data`, then those `y` elements will be treated as parameters.

Internally, NIMBLE reparameterizes this gamma distribution:

y[i,t] ~ dgamma(shape = omega[z[i,t], 1],

model$omega
